title: Does Opening Your Phone Void the Warranty? What to Check in India
html:
It depends on what your warranty says, and on what caused the fault. Read the terms. Google's own India warranty, for example, excludes damage caused by unlocking the bootloader or altering the firmware, and says servicing by anyone other than its authorised technicians voids coverage. Opening a phone is not itself damage, but if a repair or a modification causes the fault, expect the claim to be refused, and know where to complain if you think the refusal is wrong.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. This is general information, not legal advice.

Sources last checked: 10 Oct 2026.

Read the warranty terms first

A warranty is a set of promises with exclusions. Google's Hardware Limited Warranty for India gives one year from the date of purchase. It excludes damage caused by unlocking the bootloader, installing an alternative bootloader or otherwise altering the phone's firmware or operating system. It also excludes water damage and other external causes, and it says servicing other than by Google authorised technicians voids coverage. Other makers have their own terms. Find yours in the box, on the maker's site, or in the warranty card.

Rooting and unlocking the bootloader

The Android Open Source Project explains what unlocking does: moving a device from locked to unlocked wipes the data partitions, after asking you to confirm. An unlocked device shows a warning at boot and will start software that is not signed by the maker, which removes the check that normally stops that. Google's warranty excludes damage caused by this. Check your maker's terms before you do it, and back up first.

Repairs by someone else

If you use a repair shop that is not authorised, check your warranty's wording: Google's terms say servicing by non-authorised technicians voids coverage. A refusal is easiest to defend when the repair plausibly caused the fault, and hardest when the problem is unrelated. Ask the maker to say in writing which exclusion they are relying on, and which part caused the fault.

If you plan to send the phone for repair at any shop, protect your data first: what a phone repair shop can see.

If a claim is refused: India

The National Consumer Helpline can be reached on the toll-free numbers 1915 and 1800 11 4000, daily except national holidays, from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM. You can also use WhatsApp on +91 88000 01915, SMS to 8800001915, email nch-ca@gov.in, the web portal consumerhelpline.gov.in, or the NCH and UMANG apps.

Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, if the District Commission is satisfied that the goods have the defects complained of, section 39 lets it direct the other party to remove the defect, replace the goods with new goods free of defect, or return the price along with interest, among other orders such as compensation for loss or injury caused by negligence. Under section 69, a complaint must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. The Commission can still accept a late complaint if you show sufficient cause for the delay, and it must record its reasons for allowing it.

The usual order is: ask the maker or seller in writing; if that fails, use the National Consumer Helpline; and if that fails, a consumer commission. Keep every message.

Keep your paper trail

  • Keep the invoice (a photo, and an email to yourself) and note the warranty end date.
  • Note the serial number and IMEI somewhere other than the phone.
  • Photograph the phone before you open it or hand it over.
  • Keep every complaint and reply in writing.

What to do next

  1. Find and read your warranty's exclusions.
  2. Back up before any repair or modification, and photograph the phone.
  3. If a claim is refused, ask for the reason and the part in writing, then use the helpline.
